claims.note: Names the hackathon MVP as the verified knowledge ledger for autonomous AI agents.
Defines the ledger as a cumulative knowledge system powered by verification, traceability, and governance.
Tightens the problem to the distinction between agent memory and trustworthy knowledge.
Reduces observability to its core question: what happened.
Reduces memory and ontology to their core question: what should be carried forward.
Names Proofpress as the third layer above observability and memory plus ontology.
Defines the Proofpress layer by the reliance question it answers.
Condenses the product mechanism into a traces-to-governed-knowledge progression.
Frames the interactive graph as the decision about which conclusions become knowledge.
Places version trust state directly inside the finance analyst workflow.
Summarizes the portable trust receipt as run, evidence, reviewer, and scope traveling with a conclusion.
Introduces the admin governance graph as the surface for deciding what enters shared knowledge.
Raises the closing vision from autonomous agents to self-improving companies.
Removes the long bad-summary explanation to keep the problem slide focused.
Removes the separate ledger-tab explanation from the product demo slide.
Removes the first separate evidence-tab card because evidence is now visible in node receipts.
Removes the second separate evidence-tab card because review state is now visible in the graph.
Removes the third separate evidence-tab card because reliance state is now visible in the graph.
Replaces the prose governance queue with a compact admin governance graph.
Replaces the admin-role explanation with a visual current-review-rejected decision flow.
Removes the repetitive closing paragraph so the final vision and tagline carry the close.

context.why: Tighten the hackathon story around the verified knowledge ledger, simplify the product graph, add finance trust-state product proof, and close on the self-improving-company vision.
